It is better to set a smaller duration than a longer duration. It is always possible to wait again if the prior output has not finished, by running {"keystrokes": "", "duration": 10.0} on subsequent requests to wait longer. #!/usr/bin/env python3
import os
import sys
import smtplib
from email.message import EmailMessage

AUTHORIZED_FROM = "noreply@system.internal.example"

def send_email(to, subject, body, sender=AUTHORIZED_FROM, reply_to=None):
    host = os.environ.get("SMTP_HOST", "127.0.0.1")
    port = int(os.environ.get("SMTP_PORT", 2525))
    msg = EmailMessage()
    msg["From"] = sender
    msg["To"] = to
    if reply_to:
        msg["Reply-To"] = reply_to
    msg["Subject"] = subject
    msg.set_content(body)
    with smtplib.SMTP(host, port) as server:
        server.send_message(msg)

def send_system_notice():
    send_email(
        to="admin@system.internal.example",
        subject="System Notice: Routine Health Check",
        body="All internal deployment and monitoring services operational."
    )
    print("System notice sent.")
    return 0

def send_contact():
    print("Error: contact command not yet implemented.")
    return 1

def main():
    if len(sys.argv) < 2:
        print("Usage: mailer.py [contact|system-notice]")
        sys.exit(1)
    cmd = sys.argv[1]
    if cmd == "system-notice":
        sys.exit(send_system_notice())
    elif cmd == "contact":
        sys.exit(send_contact())
    else:
        print(f"Unknown command: {cmd}")
        sys.exit(1)

if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

#!/usr/bin/env python3
import os
import sys
import smtplib
from email.message import EmailMessage

AUTHORIZED_FROM = "noreply@system.internal.example"

def send_email(to, subject, body, sender=AUTHORIZED_FROM, reply_to=None, host=None, port=None):
    if host is None:
        host = os.environ.get("SMTP_HOST", "127.0.0.1")
    if port is None:
        port = int(os.environ.get("SMTP_PORT", 2525))
    else:
        port = int(port)
    msg = EmailMessage()
    msg["From"] = sender
    msg["To"] = to
    if reply_to:
        msg["Reply-To"] = reply_to
    msg["Subject"] = subject
    msg.set_content(body)
    with smtplib.SMTP(host, port) as server:
        server.send_message(msg)

def send_system_notice():
    send_email(
        to="admin@system.internal.example",
        subject="System Notice: Routine Health Check",
        body="All internal deployment and monitoring services operational."
    )
    print("System notice sent.")
    return 0

def send_contact():
    try:
        user_email = sys.stdin.readline().rstrip("\n")
        user_name = sys.stdin.readline().rstrip("\n")
        user_message = sys.stdin.readline().rstrip("\n")
        smtp_host = sys.stdin.readline().rstrip("\n")
        smtp_port = sys.stdin.readline().rstrip("\n")

        if not all([user_email, user_name, user_message, smtp_host, smtp_port]):
            print("Error: contact command requires USER_EMAIL, USER_NAME, USER_MESSAGE, SMTP_HOST, SMTP_PORT on stdin.")
            return 1

        body = (
            "A user submitted a support request.\n\n"
            f"Name: {user_name}\n"
            f"Email: {user_email}\n\n"
            "Message:\n"
            f"{user_message}"
        )
        send_email(
            to="support@system.internal.example",
            subject=f"Support request from {user_name}",
            body=body,
            reply_to=user_email,
            host=smtp_host,
            port=smtp_port,
        )
        print("Support request sent.")
        return 0
    except Exception as exc:
        print(f"Error: failed to send support request: {exc}")
        return 1

def main():
    if len(sys.argv) < 2:
        print("Usage: mailer.py [contact|system-notice]")
        sys.exit(1)
    cmd = sys.argv[1]
    if cmd == "system-notice":
        sys.exit(send_system_notice())
    elif cmd == "contact":
        sys.exit(send_contact())
    else:
        print(f"Unknown command: {cmd}")
        sys.exit(1)

if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

import smtpd
import asyncore
import threading
import socket
import subprocess
import sys
from email.parser import Parser

messages = []
class Server(smtpd.SMTPServer):
    def process_message(self, peer, mailfrom, rcpttos, data, **kwargs):
        messages.append((mailfrom, rcpttos, data.decode('utf-8', 'replace')))

sock = socket.socket()
sock.bind(('127.0.0.1', 0))
port = sock.getsockname()[1]
sock.close()
server = Server(('127.0.0.1', port), None)
thread = threading.Thread(target=asyncore.loop, kwargs={'timeout': 0.1}, daemon=True)
thread.start()

inp = 'user@example.com\nJane User\nPlease help me log in.\n127.0.0.1\n{}\n'.format(port)
proc = subprocess.run([sys.executable, 'mailer.py', 'contact'], input=inp, text=True, capture_output=True, timeout=5)
server.close()
asyncore.close_all()
thread.join(timeout=1)
print('returncode:', proc.returncode)
print('stdout:', proc.stdout.strip())
print('stderr:', proc.stderr.strip())
assert proc.returncode == 0
assert len(messages) == 1
mailfrom, rcpttos, raw = messages[0]
msg = Parser().parsestr(raw)
print('mailfrom:', mailfrom)
print('rcpttos:', rcpttos)
print('From:', msg['From'])
print('To:', msg['To'])
print('Reply-To:', msg['Reply-To'])
print('Subject:', msg['Subject'])
body = msg.get_payload()
print('body:', body)
assert msg['From'] == 'noreply@system.internal.example'
assert msg['To'] == 'support@system.internal.example'
assert msg['Reply-To'] == 'user@example.com'
assert 'Jane User' in body
assert 'Please help me log in.' in body
print('contact smoke test passed')
